lines.text: If you have an anxious attachment style, you know this feeling. They take too long to text back, and your brain starts writing the worst story.
lines.say11: [tense, quiet] If you have an anxious attachment style, you know this feeling. [pause] They take too long to text back... and your brain starts writing the worst story.

lines.text: Here's every coping move, ranked from what makes it worse to what actually works. And the S tier is the one almost nobody does.
lines.say11: Here's every coping move, ranked... from what makes it worse, to what actually works. [pause] And the S tier is the one almost nobody does.

lines.text: F tier. Checking if they're online. It feels like relief, but every check teaches your brain the danger is real.
lines.say11: F tier. [beat] Checking if they're online. It feels like relief... but every check teaches your brain the danger is real.

lines.text: D tier. The double text. Attachment experts call it protest behavior. A bid for closeness that usually pushes people away.
lines.say11: D tier. The double text. [knowing] Attachment experts call it protest behavior. A bid for closeness that usually pushes people away.

lines.text: C tier. Distracting yourself. It works, for about twenty minutes. Then the feeling comes back louder.
lines.say11: C tier. Distracting yourself. It works... for about twenty minutes. [pause] Then the feeling comes back louder.

lines.text: B tier. Naming the feeling. In brain scans, putting an emotion into words calmed the amygdala, your alarm system. So say it. I feel abandoned right now.
lines.say11: B tier. Naming the feeling. In brain scans, putting an emotion into words calmed the amygdala, your brain's alarm system. [softly] So say it. I feel abandoned right now.

lines.text: A tier. The physiological sigh. Two breaths in through the nose, one long breath out. In a Stanford study, five minutes a day lifted mood more than meditation.
lines.say11: A tier. The physiological sigh. [slowly] Two breaths in through the nose... one long breath out. [normal] In a Stanford study, five minutes a day lifted mood more than meditation.

lines.text: And S tier. Asking for what you need, before the panic starts. Not, why are you ignoring me. But, I feel calmer when we check in at night. Can we do that?
lines.say11: [warm] And S tier. Asking for what you need... before the panic starts. Not, [annoyed] why are you ignoring me? [warm, gentle] But, I feel calmer when we check in at night. Can we do that?

lines.text: Studies show that with a responsive partner, anxious attachment can become more secure over time. It's not a life sentence.
lines.say11: [reassuring] Studies show that with a responsive partner, anxious attachment can become more secure over time. It's not a life sentence.

lines.text: So which tier are you stuck in right now? Comment F to S.
lines.say11: [curious] So which tier are you stuck in right now? Comment... F to S.
